---
title: "Random number generator"
---

::: {.status-box .status-complete}
**Status: Documented and implemented**

This is a native ResearchOS calculation capability. It is intended as a general-purpose random source and as a foundation for later allocation and block randomisation modules.
:::

## Purpose

Generate one or more random numbers with configurable range, step size and seed behaviour.

The capability supports:

- secure-random generation for ordinary use;
- fixed-seed generation for reproducible testing or deterministic allocation sequences;
- integer-like or stepped numeric ranges.

## Capability ID

- `random.number.generate`

## Inputs

| Input | Description |
|---|---|
| `input_count` | Number of random values to generate. |
| `input_min` | Minimum possible value. |
| `input_max` | Maximum possible value. |
| `input_step` | Step size between possible values. |
| `input_seed_mode` | `secure_random` or `fixed_seed`. |
| `input_seed` | Seed text used when `input_seed_mode='fixed_seed'`. |

## Example intent calls

### One secure random integer

```text
com.example.researchos.EXECUTE_METHOD(method_id='random.number.generate',input_min='1',input_max='100',input_step='1',return_mode='flat')
```

### Five reproducible values

```text
com.example.researchos.EXECUTE_METHOD(method_id='random.number.generate',input_count='5',input_min='1',input_max='10',input_step='1',input_seed_mode='fixed_seed',input_seed='study001',return_mode='flat')
```

## Returned fields

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `random_status` | `succeeded` or `failed`. |
| `random_numbers_json` | JSON array of generated values. |
| `random_numbers_csv` | Comma-separated values. |
| `random_first_number` | First generated number, convenient for simple callers. |
| `random_count` | Number of generated values. |
| `random_min` | Minimum used. |
| `random_max` | Maximum used. |
| `random_step` | Step size used. |
| `random_seed_mode` | Seed mode used. |
| `random_seed` | Seed text when fixed-seed mode is used. |
| `random_algorithm` | Underlying random source. |
| `random_generated_time_iso` | Generation time. |
| `random_error` | Error message, if generation failed. |

## Notes

For trial allocation, this capability should be treated as a low-level primitive. More formal randomisation methods should add allocation concealment, block definitions, audit trails and protocol-specific constraints on top of this generator.
